text:
**What it is:** Sequence is an architecture scan and chat tool for your software project.

**Who it is for:** Developers who want to understand how their codebase is structured and how different parts depend on each other.

**Why it exists:** It reads your actual repository code into a live architecture graph so you can see real connections between services, files, and modules without relying on assumptions or a model.

**How it works:**
1. The tool scans your repository for imports, calls, routes, and manifest lines.
2. It maps those connections into a graph of services, modules, and files.
3. You use it to ask questions about how your system works, and the tool cites real file paths and lines for each answer.
4. Any new or proposed parts stay dashed until they're confirmed in the scanned code.
5. The graph runs entirely on your machine; nothing leaves unless you connect a key.

**Advantages:** It gives you a transparent, up-to-date view of your architecture instead of relying on static documentation. Every edge in the graph traces to actual code, so you can trust what you see. Changes in your code are immediately reflected where they connect.
